For an object (S), its '''centre of gravity''' $G_g$ is at:

{{#content:Q2041}}

=== Uniform gravitational field ===

In a uniform gravitational field,

$$
\begin{cases}
\overrightarrow{OC_g}\times \int_S \vec g(M)\,dm=\int_S \overrightarrow{OM}\times \vec g(M)\,dm \\
\vec g(M) = \vec g
\end{cases} \\
\therefore \overrightarrow{OC_g}\times \vec g \int_S\,dm=\int_S \overrightarrow{OM} \,dm\times \vec g \\
\overrightarrow{OC_g}\int_S\,dm\times \vec g =\int_S \overrightarrow{OM} \,dm\times \vec g \\
\overrightarrow{OC_g}\int_S\,dm=\int_S \overrightarrow{OM} \,dm\\
$$

Recall for the centre of inertia $C$ we have:

{{#content:Q2039}}

Therefore,

$$
C_g=C
$$

i.e., the centre of gravity and inertia coincides.
